article_content: Nurse Amber Vinson has successfully recovered from Ebola, a deadly virus she contracted while treating 'patient zero' Thomas Eric Duncan. After being admitted to Texas Health Presbyterian Hospital with symptoms, Vinson was transferred to Emory University Hospital in Atlanta for further treatment and care. Following a remarkable recovery, she has been declared Ebola-free by medical professionals and is set to be discharged. Vinson's recovery comes exactly two weeks after her initial admission, marking a significant milestone in the fight against the disease. As the second Dallas nurse to recover from Ebola, Vinson's experience serves as a beacon of hope for those affected by the virus.

article_content: England's manager, Roy Hodgson, has called on the nation to support his team as they prepare to face Italy in their World Cup opener on Saturday. Hodgson is confident that the team will make the country proud with their performance in the tournament, which begins against Cesare Prandelli's Italian side in Brazil. He has emphasized the importance of encouragement from fans back home, stating that it is crucial for the team's success. 'We want people to believe in us, we want to give them something to cheer about,' Hodgson said. The team's captain, Steven Gerrard, has also expressed his pride in leading the team, saying he trusts his teammates and believes in their abilities. Gerrard's dream has always been to play for England and Liverpool, and he considers captaining the team at the World Cup in Brazil to be the pinnacle of his career. The team is ready to give their all and make the country proud.
